task_production_rates.name: Install full kitchen floor protection for spray
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Canvas drop cloths + tape edges. Full room coverage for spray method. Kitchen floors are high-value (hardwood, tile) — careful tape-down.

task_production_rates.name: Install perimeter floor protection for brush
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Drop cloth runners at cabinet base only. Brush method — no full room coverage needed.

task_production_rates.name: Protect countertop surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Kraft/rosin paper + tape + plastic sheeting for spray. High-value surfaces (granite, quartz) — tape edges carefully to prevent paint migration underneath. Do NOT use drop cloths alone.

task_production_rates.name: Mask backsplash
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Careful edge work around tile grout lines. Green tape edge seal against tile for clean line. Paper or plastic below upper cabinets.

task_production_rates.name: Mask walls for spray overspray
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Plastic sheeting (1 mil) taped to walls. Full wall coverage for spray method. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Mask ceiling for spray overspray
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Plastic sheeting taped to ceiling perimeter. Pre-taped masking film for efficiency. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Mask appliances in spray zone
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~15-25 min per appliance. Plastic sheeting wrapped around appliance + tape. May need to pull appliance away from cabinet for frame access. Spray only. Conditional — atypical for NC (appliances usually not installed).

task_production_rates.name: Mask sink plumbing in base cabinet
task_production_rates.notes: Per room with sink base. Plastic wrap around plumbing fixtures, protect shut-off valves.

task_production_rates.name: Remove switch plates and mask electrical
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Remove outlet/switch plates (bag with hardware). Mask under-cabinet light fixtures with tape and paper.

task_production_rates.name: Remove all cabinet hardware, bag, label
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr (hardware pieces). ~1.5-2 min per piece including labeling and bagging. Hinges, pulls, knobs, soft-close mechanisms. Label bags by location (Upper Left Door 1, etc.).

task_production_rates.name: Remove cabinet doors and label
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~3-4 min per door including label, unhinge, set on sawhorses/pyramids. Hardware already removed.

task_production_rates.name: Remove cabinet drawers and label
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~2.5-3 min per drawer. Lighter and faster than doors. Pull drawer, release slides if applicable, label, set on sawhorses.

task_production_rates.name: Clean all surfaces of construction dust
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Tack cloth or damp wipe all surfaces — face frames, cabinet interiors, removed doors/drawers. Kitchen environments trap dust. More thorough than trim or wall prep.

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes on face frames

QT3.notes: Fill obvious holes. Spackle, level off.

QT4.notes: Fill all visible holes. Sand flush 220.

QT5.notes: Fill every hole regardless of size. Angled light check.

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Face frame nail holes from installation. NC overfill-sand-flush method. More fastener density on frames than on doors.

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes on doors

QT5.notes: Fill every hole, perfect flush, angled light

task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Flat on sawhorses — easy access. Fewer holes than frames (mainly hinge/pull fastener holes).

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes on drawer fronts

QT5.notes: Fill every hole, perfect flush, angled light

task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Drawer fronts smaller than doors with fewer fastener points. ~0.7x door fill time.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk cabinet-to-wall joints

QT5.notes: Invisible caulk joints, perfect tooling, zero visible bead

task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. qt_scaled. Face frame to wall (sides/top), crown molding to cabinet, filler strip to wall, end panel to wall, toe kick to floor.

task_production_rates.name: Sand face frames and box surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Initial prep sand on bare or factory-primed surfaces. Narrow frame members require careful hand sanding. Toe kick is awkward low access.

task_production_rates.name: Sand cabinet doors
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Flat on sawhorses — easy access. Rigid block on flat faces. Profile edges on shaker/raised panel require flexible approach. Apply door_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Sand cabinet drawer fronts
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Smaller than doors — ~0.7x door sanding time. Same technique. Apply door_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Sand filled areas smooth
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Sand filled fastener holes and caulk lines flush with surrounding surface. QT5 requires angled light verification.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum floor after sanding
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Floor area. HEPA vacuum for dust control — critical in kitchen environment before coating.

task_production_rates.name: Prime face frames and box surfaces

spray.notes: HVLP or fine-finish airless. Horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles.

brush.notes: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush. Roll and Tip on end panels.

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Conditional: substrate_state=SS_BARE. Primer type substrate-driven (MDF step 2 latex, wood acrylic, tannin-block). Narrow frame members slow spray vs open surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Prime cabinet doors flat on sawhorses

spray.notes: HVLP spray, face and edges. Horizontal — gravity-assisted leveling.

brush.notes: Roll and Tip. Mini foam roller to apply, brush to tip.

task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. Conditional: substrate_state=SS_BARE. Flat orientation on sawhorses/pyramids. Apply door_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Prime drawer fronts flat on sawhorses

spray.notes: Smaller than doors, faster per unit

brush.notes: Roll and Tip on flat surface

task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. Conditional: substrate_state=SS_BARE. ~0.7x door time. Apply door_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Prime cabinet interiors (spray)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Spray-only in practice — access too constrained for brush. Angle gun into cabinet box, work back wall forward, ceiling down. Upper cabinets faster than lower (less bending). Conditional: scope=full_with_interior AND substrate_state=SS_BARE.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on frames
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. HVLP or fine-finish airless. Horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles per FFD. End panels are fast (large flat). Toe kick slower (low, awkward). Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on frames
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush on narrow members. Roll and Tip on end panels. Waterborne alkyd STRONGLY recommended for open time. Brush only.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on doors
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Flat on sawhorses — gravity-assisted leveling. Spray face then edges. Light even coats. ~5-6 min per door. Apply door_style modifier. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on doors
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Flat on sawhorses. Roll and Tip per FFD SS15.6. Thin to Win per SS15.11.3. ~10 min per door. Apply door_style modifier. Brush only.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on drawer fronts
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Smaller than doors — ~0.7x door time. Same technique. Apply door_style modifier. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on drawer fronts
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Roll and Tip on flat surface. ~0.7x door time. Apply door_style modifier. Brush only.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on interiors
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Always QT3 regardless of exterior tier (AWI semi-exposed standard). Spray-only in practice. Awkward angles slow production. Conditional: scope=full_with_interior.

task_production_rates.name: Clean work area between coats
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove dust and debris from floor protection, countertop covers, sawhorse area.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect previous coat
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Inspect frames, doors, drawers in one pass. QT3: quick scan at 6 ft. QT4: systematic 3-ft inspection, mark defects. QT5: lighted critical inspection at arm's length, zero tolerance. Check for runs on vertical frame members, leveling on flat doors, dust nibs.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats on frames

QT5.notes: Thorough full sand 220-320 grit, uniform scratch

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Rigid block on end panels. Flexible approach on narrow stiles/rails. Narrow frame members make thorough sanding slower than open surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats on doors
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Flat on sawhorses. Rigid block on flat face. Profile edges on shaker/raised panel. Apply door_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats on drawers
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. ~0.7x door time. Apply door_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats on interiors
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Always QT3 — spot sand only. Awkward interior access. Conditional: scope=full_with_interior.

task_production_rates.name: Patch and repair defects
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Fill, sand, and spot-prime defects found during inspection. Scope increases with tier. Covers all items (frames, doors, drawers).

task_production_rates.name: Spot coat patched areas
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat.

task_production_rates.name: Tack cloth all surfaces before next coat
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth. Cover frames, doors, drawers, and interiors (if in scope). Kitchen dust control is critical.

task_production_rates.name: Final quality inspection per tier
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Inspect all items: frame sheen uniformity, caulk line quality, door leveling/marks, drawer front finish. QT5: lighted critical inspection at arm's length, zero tolerance. Check all door fronts and drawer fronts on sawhorses.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-up defects from final inspection
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Correct remaining defects, feather into surrounding finish. QT5 may require additional coat if defects are widespread.

task_production_rates.name: Cure period — doors stored safely
task_production_rates.notes: Calendar days, NOT work hours. MANDATORY 5-7 day minimum. 7-14 days for waterborne alkyd (QT4). Doors/drawers stored safely, not touching. Cabinet boxes left open. Client informed kitchen without doors for 1-2 weeks. Engine should flag scheduling constraint.

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall all cabinet hardware
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr (hardware pieces). ~2.5 min per piece. Reinstall from labeled bags. Clean paint from screw holes if needed. Verify alignment. Account for paint film thickness on hinge mortises.

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall doors, adjust alignment
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~6 min per door. Hang door, adjust hinges, check swing clearance, verify soft-close operation. Slower than removal due to alignment verification. Paint film thickness may require hinge adjustment.

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall drawers, check slides
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~4 min per drawer. Reinstall on slides, check alignment, verify smooth operation and soft-close. Faster than doors — simpler alignment.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-up after reinstallation
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Touch-up hinge areas, pull/knob mounting points, screw-down marks, and any handling damage from reinstallation. Critical final step.

task_production_rates.name: Remove countertop protection
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Remove paper, tape, plastic from countertops. Careful removal to avoid adhesive residue on stone surfaces. Faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Remove backsplash masking
task_production_rates.notes: LF/hr. Score tape edge, pull at 45 degrees. Careful around tile grout. Faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Remove wall masking
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Remove plastic sheeting from walls. Fold inward. Spray only. ~1.5x faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Remove ceiling masking
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Remove plastic sheeting from ceiling. Spray only. ~1.5x faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Remove appliance masking
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. ~12 min per appliance. Remove plastic wrap and tape. Spray only. Faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Remove floor protection
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Fold inward to contain debris. Covers both spray (full) and brush (perimeter) teardown.

task_production_rates.name: Final vacuum of work area
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Floor area after all protection removed. Include inside cabinet boxes — dust settles during cure period.

task_production_rates.name: Clean tools and equipment
task_production_rates.notes: Per session. Clean brushes, rollers, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne. Solvent cleanup for shellac primer residue.

slab.description: Flat panel — simplest to paint by any method.

shaker.description: Recessed panel with square-profile frame. Moderate complexity — brush into corners of recessed panel.

raised_panel.description: Most complex common style. Recessed areas around raised panel require careful brush work to avoid buildup in reveals.

glass_frame.description: Frame only (glass removed or masked). Narrow frame members require careful work.

door_style_modifier.application_rule: TIME modifier. adjusted_hours = base_hours * door_style_value. Applies to door AND drawer tasks equally (drawer fronts follow same style as doors).

quality_tier_modifier.does_not_apply_to: binary tasks, protection, hardware removal/reinstall, cleanup. For tasks with rates_by_tier, the tiered rate already reflects QT — do NOT double-apply.
quality_tier_modifier.application_rule: TIME modifier. effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. QT modifiers apply ONLY to qt_scaled tasks WITHOUT rates_by_tier (those tasks pre-embed the QT effect).

height_modifier.does_not_apply_to: Door/drawer tasks (painted flat on sawhorses at ground level), interior tasks, hardware tasks, FIXED tasks, floor protection

standard_8ft.description: Upper cabinet tops at ~7 ft — reachable standing.

tall_9_10ft.description: Upper cabinet tops at ~9 ft — step ladder required.

extra_tall_11_12ft.description: Upper cabinet tops at ~11 ft — scaffold may be needed.

height_modifier.application_rule: TIME modifier. effective_rate = base_rate / height_modifier. Applies to FRAME tasks only — doors/drawers painted at ground level are NOT affected. Drives PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND input.

kitchen_complexity_modifier.does_not_apply_to: Door/drawer tasks (removed, painted separately), interior tasks, FIXED tasks

simple.description: Straight run of base or upper cabinets. Small bathroom vanity.

complex.description: U-shaped with island, multiple corner cabinets.

very_complex.description: Large custom kitchen with multiple zones, butler's pantry, etc.

kitchen_complexity_modifier.application_rule: TIME modifier. effective_rate = base_rate / complexity_modifier. Corner cabinets and island cabinets are harder to access and protect.

masking_scope_modifier.applies_to: Protection setup and teardown tasks only

brush.description: Reduced masking — no ceiling, no full wall, no appliance wrap.

masking_scope_modifier.application_rule: This modifier is INFORMATIONAL — the SOP already has separate spray/brush protection tasks via applies_when conditions. The estimation engine selects active tasks based on application_method, so this modifier is NOT applied at runtime. Documented for rate derivation transparency.
masking_scope_modifier.notes: Do NOT apply as a multiplier — task activation via applies_when handles method-specific masking scope.

coat_count.notes: Primer conditional on substrate_state=SS_BARE. Interstage runs after each coat except the final coat. Primer interstage included in count.

maximum_theoretical.scenario: QT5 + brush + raised_panel + extra_tall_ceiling + very_complex_kitchen (frame tasks)
maximum_theoretical.note: Under 4.0x threshold — valid. Note: raised_panel does not normally apply to frame tasks, so realistic max for frames is 1.5 * 1.30 * 1.30 = 2.54x.

realistic_maximum_doors.note: Door tasks not affected by height or kitchen_complexity. Maximum stacking is modest.

realistic_maximum_frames.note: Frame tasks not affected by door_style. Well under 4.0x.

estimation_notes.four_item_types: 4 paintable items: ITM_CABINET_DOOR (EA), ITM_CABINET_DRAWER (EA), ITM_CABINET_FRAME (SF), ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR (SF conditional). Doors/drawers use EA with per-unit rates. Frame/interior use SF with area rates.
estimation_notes.spray_vs_brush: Spray is preferred for all cabinet work. Spray ~1.4-2.0x faster than brush depending on task. Finish coat tasks are split by method (separate TSK_ for spray vs brush). Prime tasks provide rates_by_method. Interstage/prep tasks are method-independent.
estimation_notes.drawer_vs_door: Drawer fronts average ~0.7x the time of doors (smaller surface area, same technique). Rates reflect this ratio.
estimation_notes.interior_independence: Cabinet interiors are ALWAYS QT3 regardless of exterior tier selection (AWI semi-exposed standard). Always spray method. Interior scope is conditional on scope=full_with_interior.
estimation_notes.door_independence: Door/drawer tasks are NOT affected by height modifiers or kitchen_complexity modifiers. Doors are removed and painted flat on sawhorses at ground level — built-in geometry does not affect their rates.
estimation_notes.cure_time_constraint: Door reinstallation has 5-7 day cure constraint (7-14 days for waterborne alkyd at QT4). This is calendar days, not work hours. The cure period represents a separate mobilization — painter returns after cure to reinstall and touch up.
estimation_notes.two_mobilizations: Cabinet painting typically requires TWO separate site visits: (1) setup/prep/prime/finish/inspect, (2) return after cure for reinstall/touchup/cleanup. This is a scheduling consideration, not a rate adjustment.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. Refer to manufacturer PDS. Key constraint: 16-24 hour recoat for waterborne alkyd (BM Advance at QT4) means multi-day workflow for finish coats.
estimation_notes.pricing_structure: Cabinet painting should be priced as a PACKAGE per kitchen/room, not per individual task. PaintScope collects room-level inputs and spec calculates total hours.

assumptions.source: Research: 10-12 doors/hr spray finish QT3. Cross-referenced with SF_BUILTIN_NC_v1 door rates (10 EA/hr for built-in doors, cabinet doors similar size).
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides per-door spray finish rates. Research-based estimate.

assumptions.source: Research: 5-7 doors/hr brush finish QT3. ~55% of spray rate per standard spray-to-brush ratio.
assumptions.note: Brush cabinet doors requires Roll and Tip technique. Waterborne alkyd recommended.

assumptions.source: Research: 180-220 SF/hr spray finish QT3. Narrow frame members slower than open flat surfaces.
assumptions.note: Face frame spray rates are slower than wall/ceiling spray but faster than trim brush.

assumptions.source: Research: 90-120 SF/hr brush finish QT3. ~52% of spray rate.
assumptions.note: Brush works reasonably well on narrow frame members. End panels benefit from Roll and Tip.

assumptions.source: Research: Drawer fronts average 60-70% of door area. Same workflow structure.
assumptions.note: Small drawers (spice, utensil) are very fast. Large pot drawers approach door size. 0.7x is average.

assumptions.source: Research: condition_drivers.door_style. Cross-referenced with Fine Finish Doctrine panel door sequence SS15.11.2.
assumptions.note: Raised panel is most complex common style. Glass frame requires masking or glass removal.

assumptions.source: Research: 30-45 pieces/hr removal, 20-30 reinstall. Cabinet hardware is faster than built-in (standardized hinge types, machine screw fasteners).
assumptions.note: Modern cabinet hardware (Euro hinges, soft-close) is designed for quick removal/reinstall.

assumptions.source: Research: 15-20 doors/hr removal, 8-12 reinstall. Reinstall slower due to alignment verification.
assumptions.note: Paint film thickness on hinge mortises may require adjustment during reinstall.

assumptions.value: Prime 175, finish 150 SF/hr (spray only, always QT3)
assumptions.source: Research: prime 150-200, finish 130-170 SF/hr. Awkward angles slow production.
assumptions.note: Interior surfaces are spray-only in practice. Always QT3 per AWI semi-exposed standard.

assumptions.source: Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine.md v1.1 (room complexity). Adapted for kitchen-specific layout factors.
assumptions.note: Kitchen complexity affects frame painting and protection tasks. Doors/drawers unaffected (removed from kitchen).
